biggest_catch: Pulse is a real, official program — but Survey Junkie publishes no concrete payout figure for it in any official source. The official copy says only that it earns you 'automatic rewards' — no points, no dollars, no schedule — while the '100 points for 30 days' figure circulating online comes from third-party reviews, not the company. Sharing your browsing data for an undisclosed amount is a bad trade to recommend.
catches: No official payout amount: 'automatic rewards' is the entire official statement — no points, dollars, or schedule published.
The widely-cited 100-points-for-30-days figure is third-party (medium.com review, surveypolice); Survey Junkie's own pages do not state it.
Pulse shares your browsing behavior (searches, sites visited, apps used, shopping, ads seen) with brands for market research — a real privacy trade.
You must keep the extension/app enabled for 30 days to earn anything — uninstall early and you get nothing (third-party documented).
Points live in the Survey Junkie system (100 pts = $1, $5 minimum redeem — third-party documented), so Pulse earnings are only as good as Survey Junkie's own redemption terms.

c1.evidence: Survey Junkie by DISQO — real operating company; SJ Pulse is the official add-on program confirmed on surveyjunkie.com ('an add-on where you automatically share your digital browsing behaviors in exchange for rewards').

eligibility: Survey Junkie member (US, Canada, Australia, UK; 16+/18+ by country); install SJ Pulse browser extension or opt in via the Survey Junkie app; keep enabled 30 days.
notes: Official program, real company — but rejected under the strict rule: 'automatic rewards' with no amounts is not a concrete payout term. Note also the catalog's R0185 steps describe game-offer milestones, which is the wrong flow for a passive data-sharing program — the route's own steps need rewriting if it is ever re-verified.
